status: Shared vertex allocation ownership and world capacity shrink adopted; GPI-S2 remains in progress
selection: RetainedBuffer reused all maximum-seen capacity on nonempty smaller replacements. Baseline regression demonstrates a 60-byte live payload retaining a 256-byte GPU allocation.
production_paths: RetainedBuffer<Vertex/StrokeInstance> -> VertexAllocation for Board/schematic world vertices/strokes (four slots)
ScreenBuffer -> same VertexAllocation for nine screen streams in full-frame and dialog-only rendering
competing_paths_retired: Independent GPU allocation/capacity ownership in RetainedBuffer
Duplicate GPU allocation/grow/shrink creation in ScreenBuffer
Maximum-seen world capacity retained across arbitrary nonempty shrink
change: VertexAllocation owns the buffer handle and mapped initialization. Source owners preserve immutable-Arc or exact-screen-content identity. Reuse capacity between live payload and four times live payload; replace outside that interval. Empty streams drop the source/allocation owner. Renderer/device teardown drops all owners. GPU buffer size is allocation authority instead of a separately mutable capacity counter.
bounds: Thirteen production slots share the input-relative four-times-live capacity policy, with WGPU alignment for sub-word payloads. Screen CPU snapshot caps remain 256 KiB per slot (nine slots); retained CPU source ownership remains one Arc per slot. This is not an absolute admitted-workload byte ceiling or driver/in-flight residency measurement.

proof.baseline: New test on baseline production code fails: allocation size 256 versus expected 60 after below-quarter occupancy. Test-only patch and failed log retained.
proof.retained_gpu: Actual GPU readback passes cold/warm/equal-size replacement plus 256->64 boundary reuse, 64->60 shrink to 60, correct replacement bytes, warm zero upload and clear/reset. Existing retained-source lifetime checks remain.
proof.screen_gpu: Existing actual screen-owner readback passes exact reuse, dirty replacement, snapshot cap/bypass, capacity shrink, empty and reset against the common allocator.
proof.bundle_gpu: Actual Renderer draws a retained world with 8x vertex storage then its original source: GPU capacity shrinks to original payload, encoded bundle rebinds, and unchanged subsequent frame keeps the bundle. Camera/visibility/binding/close cases remain passing.
proof.dialog_gpu: Actual dialog warm/evicted/restored upload pixel comparison passes after allocation migration.
proof.native: Fresh release X11 MAIN zoom-in/out plus GLOBAL/PROJECT/NEW startup/presentation/close pass, exit zero. Native resource replacement accounting/driver memory not qualified.
proof.build_lint: Offline guarded release and renderer library/tests Clippy pass.
proof.governance: Source health, dependency authority, parity, traceability/spec/project, diff and staged formatting checked before commit.
proof.app_scope: No app source changes or full app suite rerun. Known terminal lineage/convergence issues remain open.

limits: No numerical speedup or process/driver memory claim. Transient in-flight resources and externally held bundle/buffer handles are not counted as released physical GPU memory by these tests.
Absolute workload byte caps and complete CPU/GPU/native accounting, actual device-recreation qualification and full backend/scale/performance qualification remain open.
Resolved schematic content performance remains unqualified; shared Board/schematic resource code adoption does not admit a fixture.
World and screen source identity semantics, screen vertex-granular dirty ranges, text/AA/pass order, dependency/license and resize boundaries remain unchanged. S2 remains in progress.
